Package neqsim.process.equipment.ejector

Class EjectorFixedGeometrySolver

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.ejector.EjectorFixedGeometrySolver
public class EjectorFixedGeometrySolver extends Object
Fixed-geometry (off-design) solver for gas ejectors.

The geometry is given by the nozzle throat area and the constant-area mixing section area. The motive mass flow is the choked flow of the nozzle, the entrained flow follows from the one-dimensional constant-pressure mixing model (Keenan et al. 1950, ESDU 86030) with nozzle, suction, mixing and diffuser efficiencies, and the discharge pressure follows from the momentum and energy balances. Real-gas states are obtained with PS and PH flashes.

  1. Motive flow: maximum of the mass flux rho v over the throat pressure (isentropic efficiency of the nozzle) times the throat area.
  2. At a mixing pressure the primary jet occupies A_p = m_p / (rho_p v_p); the entrained stream gets the remaining mixing area and accelerates from the suction pressure with the suction nozzle efficiency. The maximum over the mixing pressure is the critical (double-choked) entrainment.
  3. Momentum balance with the mixing efficiency, energy balance for the static mixed state.
  4. The diffuser recovers diffuser-efficiency times the kinetic energy of the mixed stream. The critical back pressure is reached by isentropic compression from the mixed static state to that enthalpy. For a discharge pressure above it the mixing pressure rises until the recoverable pressure equals the discharge pressure (entrainment falls); if this is not possible at any entrainment the ejector is in breakdown.

The ejector entrains vapour only; for a two-phase suction or motive stream the vapour phase is used.
